 2025:KER:37322 LA.APP. NO. 97 OF 2024  4  JUDGMENT 1.
This Land Acquisition Appeal is filed by claimants 1 to 3 in L.A.R. No. 38/2019 of the District Court-II, Thiruvananthapuram.

The Reference was under Section 76 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') for apportionment of the compensation deposited in the Court.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Reference Court found that the claimants Nos.4 to 6 are entitled for the deposited amount.
Challenging the said judgment of the Reference Court, the present Appeal is filed under Section 74 of Act.

2. When this matter came up for hearing, the learned counsel for the contesting party respondents 1 to 3 / 2025:KER:37322 LA.APP. NO. 97 OF 2024 claimants 4 to 6, Sri.Girish Kumar pointed out that Section 74 does not provide appeal against the award passed under Section 76 of the Act and that it provides appeal only against the award under Section 69 of the Act.
In view of the said contention, the appellants have filed I.A. No. 3/2025 praying refund of Court Fee on rejection of the appeal, since the appeal is not maintainable under Section 74 of the Act.

The said prayer of the appellants was strongly opposed by the counsel for the contesting respondents, contending that as per Section 66 of the Kerala Court Fees and Suit Valuation Act, there is no provision to refund the Court Fee when an appeal is rejected.

entities.text: Kerala Court Fees and Suit Valuation Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. On going through Section 66 of the Kerala Court Fees and Suit Valuation Act, it is seen that Section 2025:KER:37322 LA.APP. NO. 97 OF 2024 66 does not deal with rejection of appeal.

entities.text: Kerala Court Fees and Suit Valuation Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the appellant Sri.Beyon.T.Varghese cited the decision of this Court in Thomas and Others v. Dr. Sudha and others 2010 (4) KHC 575, in which it is held that Court Fee is refundable when second appeal is rejected as not maintainable.

entities.text: Thomas and Others v. Dr. Sudha and others 2010 (4) KHC 575
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The learned counsel further cited the decision of the Punjab & Haryana High Court in Joginder Singh v. Sant Kaur 1999 0 Supreme(P&H)153, in which it is held that when the Regular First Appeal is found maintainable, the appellant is entitled to get refund of the entire Court Fee.
4.
